resources.name: Kamal
resources.description: Official CLI for building images, provisioning Docker hosts, and deploying applications over SSH.
resources.details: Kamal coordinates Docker image builds, registry pushes, rolling deployments, accessories, and proxy health checks on servers you control.
resources.best_for: You want the canonical Kamal tool and deployment workflow.
resources.caveat: Kamal 1/MRSK tutorials describe Traefik and configuration that differ from current Kamal.

resources.name: kamal-proxy
resources.description: Reverse proxy powering health-checked traffic switching during modern Kamal deployments.
resources.details: Kamal Proxy routes requests to application containers and participates in the cutover once a new release responds to health checks.
resources.best_for: You need to understand routing, TLS, or zero-downtime rollout behavior.
resources.caveat: This is an infrastructure component, not a standalone deployment dashboard.

resources.name: Kamal documentation
resources.description: Official reference for installing, configuring, operating, and upgrading Kamal.
resources.details: Covers current commands, deploy.yml options, hooks, destinations, and version migrations directly from the project maintainers.
resources.best_for: You are checking exact configuration syntax or the expected behavior of a command.
resources.caveat: Choose the correct version of the docs; Kamal 1 guidance is separately maintained.

resources.name: kamal-deploy Action
resources.description: GitHub Action to run Kamal 2 deployments from CI, including destinations and optional image-push control.
resources.details: Runs Kamal from a GitHub runner and supports separate environment/config inputs and deployments using previously pushed images.
resources.best_for: You want deployments to happen after CI instead of from a laptop.
resources.caveat: Runners need SSH access and the required registry and app secrets.

resources.name: kamal-complete
resources.description: Bash, Zsh, and Fish tab completions for Kamal subcommands and flags.
resources.details: Supplies shell completion files and install instructions for common interactive terminals.
resources.best_for: You use the Kamal CLI frequently and want quicker command discovery.
resources.caveat: Install the variant for your shell; the project does not change Kamal itself.

resources.name: Kamal-TUI
resources.description: Terminal user interface for exploring and running Kamal operations.
resources.details: An alternative interaction layer for Kamal operators who prefer navigable terminal screens to individual CLI commands.
resources.best_for: You are evaluating a keyboard-first operations interface.
resources.caveat: Review current command coverage and version compatibility before production use.

resources.name: kamal-panel
resources.description: Self-hosted SSH-based Kamal panel for status, logs, deployments, rollbacks, and notifications.
resources.details: Uses Kamal commands and SSH access to collect fleet state and perform operational actions; includes log views and alert rules.
resources.best_for: You run multiple apps and want a central operational interface.
resources.caveat: Treat admin access and stored SSH credentials as highly privileged.

resources.name: Helmsman
resources.description: Local browser interface experiment for Kamal operations.
resources.details: A project worth investigating as an alternative local interface for running deployment tasks.
resources.best_for: You prefer a local UI to a hosted control plane.
resources.caveat: A maintained README could not be retrieved during curation; review functionality directly.

resources.name: Shipyrd
resources.description: Team deployment dashboard fed by Kamal lifecycle hooks.
resources.details: Runs as a Kamal accessory and gathers hook-driven deployment events to show releases to collaborators.
resources.best_for: You want shared deploy status without replacing Kamal.
resources.caveat: It has hosting and storage requirements; consult the setup instructions.

resources.name: kamal-lint
resources.description: Static config linter for secrets, registry mismatches, invalid roles, and legacy proxy settings.
resources.details: Checks deploy.yml and destination overrides, and supports GitHub Actions annotations and structured output.
resources.best_for: You want config failures caught before an actual production deploy.
resources.caveat: Static linting cannot prove that servers and running workloads are healthy.

resources.name: kamal-json-schema
resources.description: Kamal 2 YAML schema providing editor autocomplete, hints, and validation.
resources.details: A JSON Schema reference that can be attached to deploy.yml through a YAML language-server comment.
resources.best_for: You want editor help while writing deployment configuration.
resources.caveat: Editor checks complement Kamal's own config validation.

resources.name: kamal-backup
resources.description: Encrypted scheduled database and Active Storage backups packaged as a Kamal accessory.
resources.details: Uses restic repositories and documented restore drills for Rails deployments, including PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite and files.
resources.best_for: You run a Rails app on Kamal and need repeatable backups and restore testing.
resources.caveat: Test a real restore and review retention and storage credentials before relying on backups.

resources.name: Rails Conductor
resources.description: Early-stage self-hosted Rails operations control plane with Kamal support.
resources.details: Brings SSH execution, deployments, backups, metrics, and alerts into one interface for Docker/Kamal and native deployments.
resources.best_for: You operate a mixed Rails infrastructure and want a self-hosted control plane.
resources.caveat: The maintainers explicitly mark some features in progress; verify maturity.

resources.name: DeployAngel
resources.description: Ruby instrumentation for post-deployment behavior checks in Rails, Hanami, and Sinatra.
resources.details: Collects aggregated application signals after releases to help confirm runtime behavior beyond a container being healthy.
resources.best_for: You need application-level evidence a deployment is behaving normally.
resources.caveat: Requires a Ruby agent and configured telemetry ingestion.

resources.name: Automated CrowdSec Kamal
resources.description: Community integration of CrowdSec security tooling with Kamal.
resources.details: Illustrates ways to add intrusion detection and response around a containerized app stack.
resources.best_for: You are evaluating host and edge security around Kamal.
resources.caveat: Test firewall and security rules on disposable infrastructure first.

resources.name: Shoestring
resources.description: Self-hosted observability that combines SSH snapshots with kamal-proxy request logs.
resources.details: Its boxwatch workflow produces HTML and agent-readable reports covering latency, errors, host resources, and container health.
resources.best_for: You have a few machines and want local diagnostics without a hosted APM bill.
resources.caveat: Requires log and SSH access; monitoring is not the same as managed alerting.

resources.name: Upstate
resources.description: Hosted Kamal production visibility with deploy receipts, observer health checks, and alerts.
resources.details: Connects the signals from hosts, components, and deployments to help owners see whether their fleet is behaving as intended.
resources.best_for: You manage several Kamal apps and want a single view of their operational health.
resources.caveat: Commercial sponsor of this directory; sponsorship does not affect inclusion or order.

resources.name: kamal-ansible-manager
resources.description: Ansible setup for Docker and Ubuntu server hardening before deploying with Kamal.
resources.details: Installs and configures Docker, Fail2ban, UFW, time sync, security updates, SSH policy and swap.
resources.best_for: You want consistent Ubuntu baseline provisioning.
resources.caveat: Review SSH/firewall changes carefully to avoid losing remote access.

resources.name: terraform-hetzner
resources.description: Terraform example separating Kamal web hosts from private accessory hosts at Hetzner.
resources.details: Creates web and data servers, SSH jump-host configuration, and optional load balancing with more web machines.
resources.best_for: You want a concrete multi-server Kamal provisioning example.
resources.caveat: Adapt its infrastructure assumptions and firewall rules before using it in production.

resources.name: kitsune-kit
resources.description: Pre-1.0 CLI for provisioning DigitalOcean Ubuntu hosts for Docker and Kamal.
resources.details: Uses init/doctor/plan/apply steps to configure a tagged Droplet, SSH, UFW, Docker, and optional data services.
resources.best_for: You want a guided DigitalOcean server setup with a reviewed change plan.
resources.caveat: Supported systems are intentionally limited; the state format may change before 1.0.

resources.name: dsd-vps-kamal
resources.description: Django Simple Deploy plugin generating Kamal configuration for an existing VPS.
resources.details: Generates deploy.yml, Dockerfile, secrets, and Django production settings, with optional full deployment automation.
resources.best_for: You use Django and want help preparing a Kamal deployment.
resources.caveat: Pre-1.0; provisioning and securing the VPS is out of scope.

resources.name: shipyard
resources.description: Opinionated Ansible, Tailscale, Cloudflare, and Caddy setup for Kamal hosting.
resources.details: Builds private networking, server roles, TLS, Postgres/Redis, backups and optional telemetry before handing application deploys to Kamal.
resources.best_for: You want a repeatable self-hosted stack rather than a series of manual VPS setup steps.
resources.caveat: It makes substantial infrastructure choices; understand the Cloudflare and Tailscale dependencies.

resources.name: Single Server
resources.description: Single-server app delivery system incorporating Kamal, Docker, GitHub, and Cloudflare.
resources.details: A more opinionated self-hosting interface built around pushing code to one Linux server.
resources.best_for: You want to compare managed-feeling single-host delivery to running Kamal directly.
resources.caveat: Its workflows are not identical to vanilla Kamal; evaluate the architecture first.

resources.name: kamalduo
resources.description: Sinatra application example for Kamal 2, including health checks and VPS walkthroughs.
resources.details: Includes /healthz, Docker setup, CI and secrets notes plus deployment instructions for multiple VPS providers.
resources.best_for: You want a concrete non-Rails Kamal 2 example.
resources.caveat: Demonstration settings are a learning aid, not drop-in production defaults.

resources.name: Kamal frontend/backend demo
resources.description: Example of separate Bun/Node frontend and backend services with a database on one Kamal host.
resources.details: Shows how multiple HTTP apps and hostnames can share a server in a configuration beyond the typical single Rails app.
resources.best_for: You deploy frontend and API services separately.
resources.caveat: The example database is provisioned but not fully exercised by the app.

resources.name: GhostCMS on Kamal and Hetzner
resources.description: Community Ghost CMS deployment example using Kamal on Hetzner.
resources.details: A reference for containerizing and deploying a CMS rather than a Ruby or Node application template.
resources.best_for: You are adapting Kamal to self-hosted content publishing.
resources.caveat: Verify current Ghost image and Kamal compatibility before reusing scripts.

resources.name: kamal-quake
resources.description: QuakeJS browser-game deployment example using Kamal.
resources.details: A playful example showing that Kamal can ship a containerized app outside its Rails origins.
resources.best_for: You want an approachable deployment demo.
resources.caveat: Educational example, not production operations tooling.

resources.name: grimmory-kamal
resources.description: Kamal configuration example for a self-hosted library application.
resources.details: A real app's deployment files that can help compare Docker and Kamal choices with your own setup.
resources.best_for: You learn best by reading other applications' deploy configs.
resources.caveat: Its configuration reflects one project's environment and may need updating.

resources.name: Embeddings inference accessory
resources.description: Example of an embeddings inference workload deployed alongside a Kamal app.
resources.details: Explores deployment of an AI-support service as an accessory-like process.
resources.best_for: You are planning an additional inference service in a self-hosted stack.
resources.caveat: Review resource consumption and persistence independently.

resources.name: django-emojivote
resources.description: Django sample application with deployment-related files.
resources.details: A small Python web app that can be inspected when exploring non-Rails Kamal practices.
resources.best_for: You want to inspect another framework's deployment layout.
resources.caveat: This is an example application, not a reusable deployment tool.

resources.name: Kamal Handbook
resources.description: Long-form handbook for learning Kamal deployment and production operations.
resources.details: A book-style alternative to collecting disconnected tutorials about server setup and day-two tasks.
resources.best_for: You prefer a structured, start-to-finish learning resource.
resources.caveat: Paid material; verify which Kamal releases are covered.

resources.name: Kamal Wiki
resources.description: Independent Kamal documentation and practical tutorial collection.
resources.details: Supplemental community writing and operational examples outside the official docs.
resources.best_for: You are looking for additional walkthroughs and alternative explanations.
resources.caveat: Check article dates; older Kamal 1/MRSK examples may no longer apply.
